name: DAMA/NaI
summary: DAMA/NaI was the DAMA programme's first large-mass NaI(Tl) dark-matter detector, searching for Galactic dark matter through annual modulation of multiyear energy spectra. DAMA/LIBRA is its successor.
detection_principle: High-purity NaI(Tl) scintillation crystals record low-energy single-hit events to search for rate variations with the phase and period expected from Earth's orbit. Annual modulation alone does not automatically exclude all environmental or instrumental explanations.

status.label: Completed
status.evidence: The collaboration states that DAMA/NaI stopped operating in July 2002 after seven annual cycles.

collaboration.participants_note: Only verified representative institutions are listed, not a complete membership roster. See the collaboration pages and author affiliations in the references.

results.summary: The collaboration reported an annual-modulation signal. Its dark-matter interpretation remains disputed, and subsequent same-target tests have not reproduced the same signal.

science_scope: Historical direct-detection experiment; the observed annual modulation must be distinguished from its interpretation as dark matter.
